task.title: Relics: project schemas with versions
task.description:
A relic is a new kind of record in Workbook, separate from tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions, transcripts and similar material, with the same history and sharing that tasks have. A relic has a title, a type, an author, links, and content made of named parts.

This story lets a project define what its relic types contain, so that agents are held to a shape when they save. Until now every type accepted anything.

## What a schema is

- One schema per relic type, such as `spec`, `plan`, `decision` or `transcript`.
- A schema says, for its type:
  - which properties the relic may or must have;
  - which part types are allowed, the fields of each, whether each has a body, and which body formats it accepts;
  - which relationship names its links may use beyond the default list, and the shape of a link pointer.
- A type with no schema stays open: it accepts anything beyond the fields Workbook enforces.

## Where schemas live

- In the shared project settings, beside statuses and priorities. They sync to everyone and cannot differ between code branches.
- Each schema version is its own stored object in the settings history. The settings document lists only each version's type, number and size, so reading statuses never reads schemas.
- Limits: one schema version is at most 64 KiB, and a type has at most 500 versions.
- Once a project saves its first schema, the settings hold a kind of change older Workbook versions do not know. An older version can still read the settings and is told to upgrade before changing them, which is the existing behavior for any newer settings change.

## Syntax

JSON Schema, limited to this documented list. A schema that uses anything else is refused when it is saved. The list can grow later and never shrink.

| Purpose | JSON Schema words |
| --- | --- |
| Kind of value | `type` (string, number, integer, boolean, object, array, null) |
| Shape of an object | `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties` (true or false) |
| Shape of a list | `items`, `minItems`, `maxItems` |
| Allowed values | `enum`, `const` |
| Size | `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minimum`, `maximum` |
| Reuse | `$ref` and `$defs`, within the project only |
| Notes for people and agents | `title`, `description` |

- A schema can reuse a definition from inside itself, or from another relic type in the same project, so one type can be composed from pieces of another.
- A reference to another type is fixed to that type's version at the moment the schema is saved. A saved schema version therefore never changes meaning.
- References to web addresses, to anything outside the project, or in a loop are refused when the schema is saved.
- Left out: pattern matching, format checks, and `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `not`.

## Versions

- Saving a schema for a type adds a new version. Every old version stays for good.
- Each relic names its type and the schema version it was written under, and stays editable under that version.
- Moving a relic to a newer version is an explicit step: `relic migrate <relic> --to <version>`. The whole relic must fit the new version. Changing a relic's type is done the same way.
- `relic list --behind` lists relics that are behind the newest version of their type.
- Relics created before this story name no schema. They stay valid until someone migrates them.

## When the schema is checked

- **On create:** the whole new relic must fit, including every required property.
- **On update:** the piece being saved (a property, a part, a link) is checked, and a required property cannot be cleared. A refused save names the rule it broke.
- **On migrate:** the whole relic must fit the version it is moving to.
- **Never on read or sync.** A relic that does not fit its schema stays readable and is flagged as not conforming. The flag is worked out for the whole relic when the index picks up a change to it.
- **Unknown version:** a relic that names a schema version this clone has not synced yet can be read. Editing it is refused until the clone syncs.
- If one side of a sync moved a relic to a new schema version and the other edited it, both apply, and the relic is flagged if it no longer fits.

The schema guides honest tools. It is not a security boundary.

## Commands

```
workbook schema list | show <type> | put <type> <file>
workbook relic migrate <relic> --to <version>
workbook relic list --behind
```

The generated agent guidelines list the project's relic types and their rules, drawn from its schemas.

## Done when

- A project can save a schema, and a save that breaks it is refused with a message naming the rule.
- An unsupported JSON Schema word, an outside reference and a reference loop are each refused when the schema is saved.
- Two valid edits that together break the schema leave a readable relic flagged as not conforming.
- Reading statuses does not read any schema object.
- Two people saving a schema for the same type at once both keep their version, and every relic still names exactly one version.
- The reference documents the supported rules and the checking points.

## Not in this story

The built-in default schemas for specs and plans, which the next story ships.

## Where the design is

The approved design is "Workbook Relics Design" (2026-11-21). It is kept out of the repository. Until "Relics: teach agents to use relics and store the design as the first relic" is done, an untracked copy sits at `specs/2026-11-21-relics-design.html` in Dylan's checkout. After that, read the relic. This description carries what the story needs, and the design wins where the two disagree.
